Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

law noun

also laws, the law, against the law, by law

classical

Tac. Germ. 19.5: bonae lēgēs
Traupman 179–180, 195

lēx, lēgis f.

noun, third declension

a law; in the plural, the laws

A particular law, passed by the people: lēgem ferre, to propose a law (Traupman 180); contrā lēgem, against a law; lēge, by law (Traupman 195).

Other words

  • jūs, jūris n. — law as a whole; right

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.1.109: jūs cīvīle (Lewis & Short); Cic. Off. 1.33: summum jūs summa injūria; Traupman 195

    The law as a body, and what is right by it: contrā jūs, against the law (Traupman 195); jūs cīvīle, the civil law, as a subject of study.

Examples

  • plūsque ibi bonī mōrēs valent quam alibī bonae lēgēs

    and good customs count for more there than good laws elsewhereTac. Germ. 19.5

  • ollīs salūs populī suprēma lēx estō

    for them the safety of the people shall be the highest lawCic. Leg. 3.8

  • ex quō illud ‘summum jūs summa injūria’ factum est jam trītum sermōne prōverbium

    hence “the strictest law is the greatest injustice” has become a common proverbCic. Off. 1.33

See also rule, case, government, state.
